Release: v1.0.0 (tag v1.0.0, published 2026-06-23)
Source archive: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/security-profiles-operator/releases/download/v1.0.0/security-profiles-operator-1.0.0.tgz
Source sha256: 01547076b054f4a77974e4d744ff55e3c6880f6e4831f986d6b03b254584522c
(The archive's contents equal deploy/helm at tag v1.0.0 apart from Chart.yaml
key order and quoting.)

Re-vendor with:
  curl -sL -o /tmp/spo.tgz <Source archive>
  echo "<Source sha256>  /tmp/spo.tgz" | sha256sum -c
  rm -rf vendor/security-profiles-operator
  tar -xzf /tmp/spo.tgz -C vendor
  then re-apply the LOCAL PATCHES below and restore this file.

Why a vendored copy rather than the upstream OCI chart: the patches below are
needed for the operator to work inside this chart's release at all.

LOCAL PATCHES (re-apply after re-vendoring):

P1 Fixed runtime namespace. Upstream 1.0.0 hard-codes namespace
   `security-profiles-operator` in all 8 CRD conversion webhooks
   (clientConfig.service.namespace) and in the cert-manager inject-ca-from
   annotations - both in crds/ and in the webhook configurations the operator
   writes at runtime (internal/pkg/manager/spod/bindata/webhook.go:183,:205).
   So every namespaced resource and every RBAC subject must live there, not in
   the parent release namespace. templates/_helpers.tpl defines
   "security-profiles-operator.runtimeNamespace"; deployment.yaml, config.yaml
   and static-resources.yaml use it for metadata.namespace and subject
   namespaces.
P2 Parent-release ownership. The meta.helm.sh/release-name literals
   (`security-profiles-operator`, 20x) become '{{ .Release.Name }}'.
   meta.helm.sh/release-namespace stays '{{ .Release.Namespace }}': those two
   annotations name the OWNING release, not where the object runs.
P3 templates/namespace.yaml (new): creates the runtime namespace with
   pod-security enforce=privileged and helm.sh/resource-policy: keep, unless
   operatorNamespace.create=false or the release itself is installed into
   that namespace. values.yaml gains operatorNamespace.create (default true).
P4 templates/apparmor-rbac.yaml (new): grants the OPERATOR ServiceAccount
   apparmorprofiles (+ /finalizers, /status). Upstream 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 omit
   it from the operator ClusterRole while the nodestatus controller reads
   AppArmorProfiles; without it profiles never reconcile.

P1-P3 were produced and render-checked by an independent reviewer
(namespace-integration.patch; three release namespaces, 8 CRDs, 20 ownership
annotations each) and applied unchanged.

NOT patched, deliberately: upstream issue #3471 (operator ClusterRole lacks
profilebindings) affects 1.0.1; no 1.0.0 operator controller uses
ProfileBinding. Re-check P4 and #3471 on every re-vendor.
